title: Gigging and recording in New York; writing for advances
summary: McRae led a small band while preferring to write, collecting advances from publishers and record companies.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Well eventually, you went out on your own, had your own band. Did you start out having a small band, or did you try to have a larger band?
Well I had a small band,

because I was playing -- just gigging around New York, you know. I was making records and just gigging from one place to another.

I more interested in writing, if I stayed in town, you know. I figured if (Inaudible) I write one good song a week, I can, you know, I can make good money, because I was getting nice advances. I could (Inaudible) just could take my time do what I wanted to do.
Like when I was writing with Charlie, we used to get good advances from our songs. Like 'Ding Dong Boogie,' we'd get like two or three hundred dollars in advance.
That was a lot of money (inaudible), you know. Now we'll just take our time. We were writing songs for different publishing companies.

Shapiro-Bernstein, Robbins -- you name it. A lot of companies. Decca -- we'd write The A&R (inaudible). (Inaudible) man call up and say, 'Look, I got a date coming up. I want you to write something for this one and that one.'
